item.title: Former NYC schools chief drops out as finalist for Chicago Public Schools CEO
item.description: With Meisha Ross Porter dropping out, just two people — interim CPS CEO Macquline King and former superintendent of East Baton Rouge Parish schools Sito Narcisse — are left.

item.title: Cherelle Parker initially wanted a 20-cent-per-ride tax on Uber. She’s decided that’s not high enough.
item.description: Philadelphia Mayor Cherelle Parker says the school district’s plan to cut hundreds of school-based positions “is not acceptable to me.” Her solution is a $1 per ride tax on rideshare services like Uber and Lyft, up from her initial proposed fee of 20 cents per ride.

item.title: NYC’s Education Dept. is releasing a long-awaited AI policy. Some schools already have their own.
item.description: Schools have embraced a wide variety of approaches, from policies outlining acceptable use, to bans, to no formal discussion of AI at all.

item.title: Will NYC schools face cuts? Lawmakers warn the answer could influence their votes on city budget
item.description: “Are we funding empty seats?” one Queens lawmaker asked as Education Department officials declined to say if they will continue propping up school budgets.

item.title: Should you red-shirt your kindergartner? The benefits don’t seem to last.
item.description: The practice of having kindergartners start school a year late peaked during the pandemic. Those students’ academic head start has already petered out, a new study says.

item.title: America is turning against college. So why are more students enrolling?
item.description: And can the enrollment boom last as artificial intelligence threatens to change the job market?

item.title: He oversaw Philadelphia school safety during a ‘dark time.’ Here’s his view as the city’s top cop.
item.description: The school district’s plan to close schools has some people worried about a spike in fights and other violence. Kevin Bethel shares his solutions for reducing fights and gun violence involving schools.

item.title: Reports of PTA conflicts prompt proposal to give Detroit schools more options
item.description: Under the current district policy, only the PTA, a national organization with state and local chapters, is recognized as an official parent organization. The change would allow parents to form independent organizations at their schools.

item.title: NYC rolls out AI school rules. Major questions are still up in the air.
item.description: NYC released preliminary AI school guidelines, but advocates and members of the city’s AI task force say key issues like privacy and oversight remain unresolved.

item.title: Memphis schools recommended for ‘corrective action’ plan for underperforming D, F schools
item.description: In Tennessee’s first school accountability hearings tied to school letter grades, Memphis school officials testified underperforming schools are heavily reliant on unlicensed teachers.

item.title: ‘Now, let’s test you’: Tennessee GOP advances bill easing voucher testing rule over Democrats’ objections
item.description: Tennessee Republicans continue to advance legislation that would roll back a four-year-old requirement for students in the Education Savings Account program.

item.title: Sito Narcisse, finalist for Chicago Public Schools CEO, faced pushback as superintendent in East Baton Rouge
item.description: Narcisse was criticized for his handling of certain issues and even sued over a college and career event, but some board members praised his leadership as “decisive.”

item.title: CMAS social studies test potentially on the chopping block as lawmakers aim to balance next year’s budget
item.description: Joint Budget Committee lawmakers will need to vote on two pieces of draft legislation that alter or eliminate the CMAS social studies test.

item.title: Here are the two applicants for the vacant seat on the Indianapolis Public Schools board
item.description: The school board will vote on who will fill the vacant District 2 seat on Thursday. The appointed person will serve in the role until the election in November.

item.title: What makes a new AP business class click with students? A veteran Indiana teacher has answers.
item.description: With over two decades of teaching under her belt, Kristin Lidstrom is piloting the AP class for Fishers students. “By the time students are making real financial decisions, they should already feel confident navigating them, not encountering the concepts for the first time,” she said.
